html:
The Unggumi are an Aboriginal people of the west Kimberley in Western Australia, in country between King Sound and the ranges to the east, near present day Derby.

Their language belongs to the Worrorran family. Neighbours on the map include the Warrwa, the Umiida, the Ngarinyin and the Bunuba. From the 1880s pastoral stations spread inland from Derby, and the Bunuba and their neighbours fought back in the 1890s. The Unggumi language has few or no speakers today. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Unggumi are an Aboriginal people of the west Kimberley in Western Australia, in country between King Sound and the ranges to the east, near present day Derby.
